# Finding $\frac{z_1}{z_2}$

## Setting Up from Condition 1

Squaring $|z_1| = |z_1 - 2z_2|$:

$$z_1\bar{z_1} = (z_1 - 2z_2)(\bar{z_1} - 2\bar{z_2})$$

Expanding the right side:

$$z_1\bar{z_1} = z_1\bar{z_1} - 2z_1\bar{z_2} - 2z_2\bar{z_1} + 4z_2\bar{z_2}$$

This simplifies to:

$$2\text{Re}(z_1\bar{z_2}) = 2|z_2|^2 \implies \text{Re}(z_1\bar{z_2}) = |z_2|^2$$

## Using Condition 2

From $z_1\bar{z_2} = \sqrt{3}(1 - i) = \sqrt{3} - \sqrt{3}\,i$, I read off:

$$\text{Re}(z_1\bar{z_2}) = \sqrt{3}$$

Therefore: $|z_2|^2 = \sqrt{3}$

## Finding the Ratio

Let $w = \dfrac{z_1}{z_2}$. Then $z_1 = wz_2$, so:

$$z_1\bar{z_2} = wz_2\bar{z_2} = w|z_2|^2$$

Substituting the known values:

$$w \cdot \sqrt{3} = \sqrt{3}(1 - i)$$

$$\boxed{w = 1 - i}$$

## Verification

- **Condition 1:** $|z_1| = |w||z_2| = \sqrt{2}\,|z_2|$ and $|z_1 - 2z_2| = |z_2||w - 2| = |z_2|\,|-1-i| = \sqrt{2}\,|z_2|$. ✓  
- **Condition 2:** $w|z_2|^2 = (1-i)\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{3}(1-i)$. ✓

$$\boxed{1-\mathrm{i}}$$
